drivingQuestion: What additional case does each inclusive 'הכל' clause come to include?
outcomeNote: Each clause receives its inclusion, including on the variant version of the mishna that teaches slaves explicitly.

segments.he: ״הַכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין״ — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? חֲדָא לְאֵתוֹיֵי כּוּתִי, וַחֲדָא לְאֵתוֹיֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּמָּד.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What is added» by the ruling of the mishna (Ḥullin 2a, 15b): «Everyone slaughters?» The Gemara explains that the mishna teaches this «once to add a Samaritan» who slaughters, i.e., his slaughter is valid. «And» the «one» other mention of this serves «to add a Jew» who is «an apostate [meshummad].»

The Gemara further asks: «What is added» by the statement of the mishna (Ketubot 110b): «Everyone» can force others «to ascend to Eretz Yisrael,» i.e., one can compel his family and household to immigrate to Eretz Yisrael?

segments.he: לְאֵתוֹיֵי עֲבָדִים, וּלְמַאן דְּתָנֵי עֲבָדִים בְּהֶדְיָא, לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִנָּוֶה הַיָּפָה לְנָוֶה הָרָעָה.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: The mishna teaches this clause «to add slaves.» If a slave wishes to ascend to Eretz Yisrael, he can force his master to either ascend with him, or to sell him to someone who will ascend, or to free him. The Gemara asks: «And according to the one who teaches slaves explicitly» in the mishna, «what» does this phrase serve «to add?» The Gemara answers that it serves «to add» the case of one who wishes to compel his family to move «from a pleasant residence» outside of Eretz Yisrael «to a noxious residence» in Eretz Yisrael.

segments.he: ״וְאֵין הַכֹּל מוֹצִיאִין״ — לְאֵתוֹיֵי עֶבֶד שֶׁבָּרַח מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ לָאָרֶץ.
segments.en: The Gemara adds that when that same mishna teaches, in its continuation: «But all may not remove» others from Eretz Yisrael, this serves «to add» the case of «a slave who fled from outside of Eretz» Yisrael «to Eretz» Yisrael. The master may not bring him back to outside of Eretz Yisrael.
